/itineraryStops/3/description.source_en:
Lunch is at a coach-friendly local restaurant en route between Nam-gu (UN Memorial) and Jung-gu (⟦G0⟧). Two typical options depending on coach routing and group preference: (1) **Dwaeji Gukbap (돼지국밥)** — Busan's signature pork-bone broth rice soup, the city's working-class comfort food since the Korean War refugee era, served with kkakdugi radish kimchi, saeujeot shrimp paste, buchu chives, and rice (~9,000–12,000 KRW per bowl), or (2) **Milmyeon (밀면)** — Busan's wheat-flour cold noodles, an adaptation of North Korean Pyongyang naengmyeon by refugees who couldn't find buckwheat in wartime Busan, served in chilled beef-broth or in spicy bibim style (~8,000–11,000 KRW). 

Both are **regional specialties unique to Busan and not commonly found in Seoul or Jeju**. **Lunch is at the guest's own expense; the stop itself is optional** — cruise passengers on a tight sail-away schedule may notify the guide at pickup and the lunch slot will be skipped, releasing ~45 minutes back to the afternoon stops. 

Vegetarian and halal-friendly options are limited at most dwaeji-gukbap restaurants — please notify the guide at booking if dietary accommodations are needed and a separate restaurant (typically a bibimbap or hansik buffet) will be substituted.

/itineraryStops/4/whyOnRoute.source_en: Busan's identity is built on seafood the way Seoul's is built on royal Joseon palace cuisine, and Jagalchi is the single most essential expression of it. It also sits at the entrance to the Nampo-dong cluster, which is why the middle of the day pivots here: Jagalchi, ⟦G1⟧ and ⟦G0⟧ are three separate stops inside a 600 m walking radius, done on foot rather than by road.
/itineraryStops/4/whyOnRoute.tm: Личность Пусана строится на морепродуктах так же, как личность Сеула — на дворцовой кухне Чосона, и Чагальчхи выражает это лучше всего. Рынок к тому же стоит у входа в узел Нампходона, и именно поэтому середина дня разворачивается здесь: Чагальчхи, ⟦G1⟧ и ⟦G0⟧ — три отдельные остановки в радиусе 600 м, которые проходят пешком, а не на колёсах.

/itineraryStops/4/description.source_en:
**⟦G0⟧ (자갈치시장)** — **Korea's largest seafood market** and one of Busan's ten landmarks — sits on the Nampo Port waterfront in Jung-gu, a 7-minute walk from Jagalchi Station (Line 1) or Nampo Station. 

The name **'Jagalchi'** comes from **'jagal' (자갈, gravel)**, after the pebbly shoreline that once lined the area. The market's modern character was forged after the **Korean War (1950–1953)**: when many men were away fighting or had been lost in combat, **widowed and displaced women — the legendary 'Jagalchi Ajumma' (자갈치 아주머니)** — became their families' breadwinners by selling fish on wooden boxes along the pierside. 

The ajumma have been the **economic and cultural soul of Busan ever since**, embodying both the city's post-war recovery story and Korea's '**jeong (정)**' culture of long-term personal trust between vendor and customer. 

The current modern **seagull-shaped main building reopened in 2006** and houses ~400 vendors across 66,000 m² gross floor area: **1F** is the live-seafood market (octopus, snow crab, abalone, sea squirt, live hagfish, mackerel, sea cucumbers, hoe-grade flounders) where guests can **buy fresh seafood by weight then take it upstairs to a 2F restaurant for a small cooking fee** — the local way to eat at Jagalchi. 

**2F** is the sashimi-and-restaurant level. The dried-seafood section (anchovies, sea laver, kelp, dried squid) extends along the outdoor pier and is the most photogenic for travel snapshots. 

**Hours 05:00–22:00 daily; CLOSED 1st & 3rd Tuesdays of each month**. **Annual Jagalchi Cultural Tourism Festival** every October. On this bus-tour the visit is a brisk 40-min walk-through with guide commentary; guests who want to linger or eat a sashimi meal upstairs should consider our small-group product, which gives ~75 min at Jagalchi.
